new_statements.quote: Acento. El acento cae en la penúltima sílaba en kallawaya, como en quechua: atasi 'mujer', qaman 'día'.
new_statements.translation: Stress. Stress falls on the penultimate syllable in Kallawaya, as in Quechua: atasi 'woman', qaman 'day'. [Corroborated by the same author in English: Muysken 2024/2025 Oxford Guide, 'Stress assignment: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable in Kallawaya, as in Bolivian Quechua'; Hannß & Muysken 2014: 'the stress in Kallawaya is on the penultimate syllable, thus resembling Quechua'.]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the word, exactly as in (Bolivian) Quechua, whose phonology Kallawaya has taken over; the examples are disyllabic citation forms (á.ta.si > atási 'woman', qáman 'day').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the visible text (snippet shows the whole 'Acento' sub-section: one sentence plus two examples).
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned in the visible text. Bolivian Quechua allows emphatic final stress and unstressed suffixes (e.g. Quechua chapter of the same volume, p. 223), but nothing of the kind is stated for Kallawaya in what could be seen; behaviour under suffixation not shown.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms; stated as a general rule for the language ('en kallawaya'), which is a Quechua-based ritual register, so the statement is effectively that Kallawaya inherits Quechua penultimate stress. Only Google Books snippet text was seen, not the printed page.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is about Kallawaya (Machaj Juyai), the ritual/secret mixed language of the itinerant Kallawaya healers of Charazani and Curva (Bautista Saavedra province, La Paz, Bolivia): Quechua grammar and phonology with a largely Puquina-derived lexicon = Glottolog call1235 / ISO caw. Not to be confused with Puquina proper (puqu1242, extinct source of the lexicon) or with the local South Bolivian Quechua (quhb / sout2991) that supplies the grammar and whose penultimate stress Kallawaya is said to share. Muysken's data come from his own 1980s fieldwork with healers of the Charazani area; Kallawaya is nobody's first language and is now reported dormant (Glottolog AES).
